name: Art Practice (Min)

rules.name: Narrative Text
rules.desc:
Curricular Flow
Students are strongly encouraged to take the required core program courses ARTSTUDI 101 ‘Foundations ‘I and ARTSTUDI 102 ‘Foundations II’ studio series, and ARTHIST 5 ‘Art and Power’ before declaring, or at least early in their minor course flow, as these provide broad understanding and context for the field.
Early in the minor, along with the core courses, students should take two introductory (100-level) elective studio courses to fulfill their four lower-level studio electives. In these lower-level courses, students explore different media and build an understanding of the scope of contemporary art practice. After completing 100-level courses, students can focus their practice via upper (200-level) elective courses in specific areas of interest. The advanced 200-level courses are designed to deepen the student’s knowledge of particular materials and techniques and stretch their understanding of conceptual issues. Experimental and challenging, these courses typically cross area boundaries. Independent study, which a permanent faculty member supervises, is also available on a case-by-case basis as a component of a student’s 200-level coursework for the degree.
Declared minors interested in taking the Art Practice Major Seminar ARTSTUDI 201 may apply for acceptance to this course, which can count as one 200-level elective if the student is accepted. Students must have completed all the ARTSTUDI 201 prerequisites (ARTSTUDI 101, ARTSTUDI 102, ARTHIST 5, and two additional 100-level studio electives) by the time the course runs to apply. The Art Practice Major Seminar is typically offered in winter quarter. Applications consist of a portfolio and statement of interest and are due to the student’s advisor by November 31. The AP faculty will review applications at the December faculty meeting and the student will be notified of acceptance by the end of autumn quarter.
Completing a full year of ITALIC can count as four credits towards either one Art History elective or one lower 100-level Art Practice elective.

children.name: Lower Level Courses
children.notes: ARTSTUDI 101 and ARTSTUDI 102 can be taken in any order.

children.name: Lower-Level Electives
children.desc: Students must complete two lower-level ARTSTUDI courses. Any 100-level ARTSTUDI course may be applied toward the lower-level Art Practice elective requirement. Current course offerings can be found on Navigate Classes.
children.notes:
Two 2-unit MFA-taught ARTSTUDI courses may be combined to satisfy one lower-level Art Practice elective.
Completing a full year of ITALIC can count as 4 units towards either one lower 100-level Art Practice elective or one Art History elective.

rules.name: Upper Level Courses
rules.desc: Students must complete two lower-level ARTSTUDI courses. Any 200-level ARTSTUDI course may be applied toward the lower-level Art Practice elective requirement. Current course offerings can be found on Navigate Classes.
rules.notes: Independent study, supervised by Art Practice faculty, is also available on a case-by-case basis and may count towards the student's 200-level electives for the minor. Independent Study must be taken for four units to apply to the minor.

children.name: Art History Courses
children.desc: Minors must complete two additional art history/critical theory elective courses. Any ARTHIST course may be applied toward the Art History elective requirement. One Film & Media Studies course may satisfy an art history/critical theory elective.
children.notes:
One of these electives may be fulfilled by a course offered by another department with advisor approval. Substitute courses should emphasize critical analysis and interpretation of art and/or film, engagement with primary and secondary sources, and the study of artistic movements, theory, or sociohistorical contexts.
Completing a full year of ITALIC can count as four credits towards either one Art History elective or one lower 100-level Art Practice elective.

grading: All required and elective courses must be taken for a letter grade.
policies:
Minors must meet with their faculty advisor and the Student Services Specialist at the start of each year to approve coursework and ensure they are meeting degree requirements.
Students are expected to pass reviews and critiques of their work throughout the quarter and participate in open studios and exhibitions as required by their art studio courses.
transferPolicy: Advanced placement test credit may not be applied toward any requirement of the minor. A maximum of one course (up to 5 units) from other universities and the Stanford Bing Overseas Program (BOSP) may be applied to the 36 total units required for the minor. BOSP courses may not count toward any required minor courses: ARTSTUDI 101 Foundations 2D, ARTSTUDI 102 Foundations 3D/4D, and ARTHIST 5 Art and Power.
reviewNotes: Every course must be taken for a letter grade. The audit checks ARTSTUDI 101 and 102, two more 100-level ARTSTUDI courses, two 200-level ARTSTUDI courses, ARTHIST 5, and two art history electives (any ARTHIST course, or at most one FILMEDIA course), toward the 36 units the minor needs. An outside art history course your advisor approves, and at most one course (up to 5 units) from another university or Bing Overseas Studies, are moved in by hand.
